title: Run the strategic intake
description: A 10-15 minute conversation about where the company is going that fills strategy.md, the document every brain starts with.
example: Run the strategic intake.
promise: A 10-15 minute interview turns where the company is going into the strategy every other piece of work reads.

title: Define our ICP
description: Chris Pawlak's interview on company fit, buying roles, awareness and readiness, kept as one working draft.
example: Define our ideal customer profile using what we already know.
promise: An interview on who buys and why, grounded in the customers already in your brain.

title: Fill in our market
description: Who we compete with, how buyers choose and where we win, drafted from the brain and the competitors you name.
example: Fill in our market document; our main competitors are Acme and Northfold.
promise: Your competitors, how buyers choose and where you win, drafted from your notes and their websites.

title: Draft our tone of voice
description: Settle whose voice it is, draft it from writing that fits, test it on one fresh email or post, then check a new chat follows it.
example: Draft our tone of voice from our website and posts.
promise: How you sound, drawn from your real writing and tested on one fresh piece.

title: Build our design system
description: Use Brian Woloszczak and Peakout's starter to build a reusable web design system from your existing brand.
example: Build our design system from our company website.
promise: Your brand as a reusable website design system, built from the site you already have.

title: Research a market
description: A short intake, then sourced desk research on market growth, segments, pains, buyers, competitors and your current right to win.
example: Assess the market for our offering in the DACH mid-market.
promise: Sourced desk research on one market, judged against your own offer and proof.
produces: A sourced report with a positioning map

title: Review unit economics
description: Check CAC, LTV, payback and retention, then decide where growth spend should go.
example: Can we spend more on growth? Here are our CAC, ARPU and churn.
promise: CAC, LTV and payback from your own numbers, ending in PUSH, FIX, STOP or MEASURE.
produces: A decision note with its inputs and gaps

title: Prepare for a meeting
description: Get a sourced brief on a person, company or topic.
example: Help me prepare for my next customer meeting.
promise: A one-page brief before a call, from everything the brain holds on the account or person.

title: Build a landing page
description: Use your offer, audience and voice to compose a campaign page from the shared design system.
example: Build a follow-up page for our event leads and show me the local preview.
promise: A campaign page written from your strategy, ICP, voice and design system.
produces: A page on your website, at a local preview

title: Choose my next task
description: Find what needs your attention and work through it.
example: What should I focus on today?

title: Tidy names and gaps
description: Settle first names without a surname, names that may be the same and required details nobody stated, one question at a time.
example: Let us do housekeeping.

title: Run a workflow
description: Start a campaign or another multi-step action from a workflow document, and let the brain track its steps and dates.
example: Start the outbound workflow for the Q4 accounts.

title: Sync the latest updates
description: Bring recent updates from your connected tools into shared knowledge.
example: Sync recent updates from my connected tools.

title: Use ZYNT
description: The news and signals on your ZYNT lists, read against what you sell: who has a reason to hear from you now.
example: Who on our ZYNT lists has a reason to hear from us now?

title: Ask or remember something
description: Use saved knowledge and keep new findings with their sources.
example: What do we know about our target customers?

title: Change our rules
description: See and edit where files go and what Codex saves and asks.
example: From now on, always ask before tagging a client.

title: Change what we keep
description: See and edit the fields kept for people, companies and products, and how they relate.
example: Every company must have a budget owner.

title: Propose an interaction
description: Describe an action you repeat in your own tool; after your APPROVE Codex does it and records it the same way every time.
example: Propose an interaction for moving a deal in HubSpot.

title: Work in a project
description: Create a project folder, or link an existing one to your brain.
example: Create a new project for our website.

title: Add a reusable section
description: Extend your shared website library with a section from a source page or a new brief.
example: Add a comparison table to our website's reusable sections.

title: Publish the website
description: Prepare a Vercel preview and release the reviewed shared website when requested.
example: Prepare a hosted preview of our website and keep its access private.

title: Set up or resume GTM Brain
description: Start onboarding or continue from the last saved step.
example: Resume my GTM Brain setup.

title: Change my preferences
description: Adjust workplace information, language or dashboard preferences.
example: Help me change my GTM Brain preferences.

title: Make a skill of your own
description: Turn a repeated workflow into a Codex skill kept in this brain, or install one from GitHub.
example: Turn what we just did into a skill.

title: Set up ZYNT
description: With ZYNT's plugin installed, the brain fills ZYNT in from what it already knows. Without it, you get the install steps.
example: Set up ZYNT for me.

title: Set up Freckle
description: Connect Freckle and build its first list of target companies and people from what the brain already knows.
example: Set up Freckle for me.

title: Set up Clay
description: Connect Clay and find the target companies and people the brain already names; enrichment asks first.
example: Set up Clay for me.

title: Set up Woodpecker
description: Connect Woodpecker, see how your campaigns perform, and save one email sequence written from the brain as a draft.
example: Set up Woodpecker for me.

title: Set up Surfer
description: Connect Surfer, get topics from what the brain knows about the market and customers, and brief the first article.
example: Set up Surfer for me.

title: Set up HeyReach
description: Connect HeyReach, see how your LinkedIn campaigns do, and get a connection note and follow-ups written from the brain.
example: Set up HeyReach for me.
